references.text: A similar practice of sending a bird away to the open field as part of the cleansing ritual for leprosy, symbolizing the removal of impurity.
The prophecy of the Lord's suffering servant who bears everyone's iniquities, a messianic parallel to the scapegoat that carries the people's sins.
The suffering servant bears the iniquities of many, a prophetic fulfillment of the scapegoat symbolism.
God casts all their sins into the depths of the sea, reflecting the image of sins being carried away to an inaccessible place.
As far as the east is from the west, the Lord has removed our transgressions from us - the same theme of complete removal of sin.
John the Baptist points to Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, a direct fulfillment of scapegoat typology.
Christ was offered once to bear many sins, fulfilling the pattern of the scapegoat on the Day of Atonement.
Christ himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, the ultimate fulfillment of the scapegoat that carries the people's sins.
